Elāpatra : m.: A mythical serpent.

A. Son of Kadrū 1. 31. 6, 2.

B. He told serpents what he heard when he crawled into the lap of his mother when the curse was pronounced by her; Brahmā had told the gods the remedy partially to avoid the effect of the curse; he therefore advised Vāsuki to give his sister Jaratkāru to give in marriage to sage Jaratkāru; their son would stop the sacrifice of snakes 1. 3

; his advice was received with joy by serpents 1. 35. 1; Brahmā informed gods that what Elāpatra had told the snakes was exactly what he had in mind; Elāpatra's advice was to the advantage of the serpents and that it would prove true 1. 35. 8, 11.

C. Elāpatra's observation on life: One who is struck by fate takes recourse to fate since he finds no other way out (daivenopahato rājan yo bhaved iha pūruṣaḥ/sa daivam evāśrayate nānyat tatra parāyaṇam 1. 34. 3).

[See Elapatra.]
